newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up on technicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up on technicals.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended up slightly Thursday in sluggish activity, with technical buying after support held early boosting the complex though prices remained in recent technical ranges.
July climbed two cents to close at $2.177 per million British thermal units. August settled 1.5 cents higher at $2.183. Most other months ended up by 0.3 to one cent.

"There's no weather and storage is comfortable, but this was more of a technical rally. I think the technicians are looking for $2.21 and $2.25 (basis July) if the physical market supports it," said one Midwest trader.

While mild weather and growing inventories are likely to cap prices near-term, few expect physical or paper markets to crumble with prospects for better summer demand just around the corner. In addition, sources said favorable summer-to-winter spreads should keep the pace of stock building brisk and lend some support.

Traders said rumors of a problem at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, helped stir early buying, but a spokesman from Sabine, the Hub operator, said there was no problem at the Hub. Later Thursday the Coast Guard said it was investigating reports of an offshore natural gas leak in Vermilion Bay.

While chart watchers differed about whether a near-term bottom was in place, many saw little reason for a breakout and expected prices to consolidate in current ranges for awhile. They pegged minor support at $2.10, with better buying likely at $2.08. Further support was seen at $2.05 and $2.00. Resistance was first in the $2.20 area and then at $2.25, $2.37 and the contract high of $2.44.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices slipped a penny or two Thursday to the low-teens. Midcon pipes were down a similar amount to the low-$2s. New York city gate prices slipped a few cents to the high-$2.30s.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip rose one cent to $2.243. NYMEX said 29,144 contracts traded, up slightly from Wednesday's revised tally of 27,265.

On the KCBT, July finished 4.2 cents higher at $2.05, while deferreds ended up by one to three cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 2.2 cents to 12.7 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 432 lots traded, up from Wednesday's total of 335.
